On a closed interval [a,b], continuity at each point can be turned into one global \delta, because finitely many local neighborhoods are enough to cover the interval. On an open interval (a,b), a function may become steeper and steeper near a missing endpoint, as 1/x does near 0 on (0,1). Then no single \delta works everywhere.
